citations.narrative:
The housing facilities are not adequately protecting the animals from injury.
During the inspection the facility representative informed APHIS officials that a weeper capuchin (Molly) was injured by a
fan two days ago. The representative stated that Molly pulled a floor fan off on elevated surface and it injured her eye.
When the animal was presented to APHIS officials the area surrounding the left eye appeared markedly swollen
obscuring the majority of the eye making it difficult to ascertain the extent of the injury. There was bruising of the area
directly above the eye and the tissue of the lower eyelid was reddened and swollen causing it to make the lower eyelid
protrude. The outer corner of the lower eyelid appeared wet with discharge. The facility representative stated she
contacted the attending veterinarian at the time of the injury and was instructed to apply cold compresses and monitor
Molly until she can be examined. APHIS Officials confirmed this instruction when speaking with the AV who stated the
animal had an appointment to be evaluated on the afternoon of 15-July-2026.
Failure to adequately ensure that housing facilities are designed and constructed so they are structurally sound can lead
to injury of the primates. The facility must ensure that housing facilities for nonhuman primates must be designed and
constructed so that they are structurally sound for the species of nonhuman primates housed in them. They must be kept
in good repair, and they must protect the animals from injury, contain the animals securely, and restrict other animals from
entering.
Corrected at the time of inspection.
This inspection and exit interview were unable to be conducted due to the availability of a facility representative.
Additional Inspectors:
Mark Sanderbeck, ANIMAL CARE INSPECTOR n
